evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor_full: Rep gives range: 'For the type of move you have, I would estimate it to be between two and a half to three and a half hours. So it's safe to budget around $660 to $864' with some personalization to 1-bed apartment
evidence_quotes.value_days_none: Saturday November 21st selected; no mention of Value Days or cheaper day alternatives
evidence_quotes.prep_and_temperature_check_none: No Save Your Ass framing about prep; no 'How do you feel about that?' asked
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check_throwaway: Rep asks 'will there be anything else?' which is administrative, not a genuine 'what's still concerning you' check
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask_never: No rate lock mentioned, no explicit ask for business. Call ends with customer declining to proceed due to trip fee objection; rep offers to send quote if customer changes mind but never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?'

top_strength: Rep gathered detailed logistics probing (floor, elevator access, unit number, square footage, walking distances, inventory list including box count) in a methodical way that would support accurate estimating.
coaching_note: The call never entered the Two Promises step at all—the rep jumped straight from quid pro quo into logistics probing, skipping the reliability and damage coverage promises that should have answered the customer's unstated concerns; additionally, no two-concerns question was asked to surface what mattered to this customer before diving into details.
